headline: High risk: Flowise can write broad filesystem/network outputs while slim runs privileged shell-based image analysis, creating dangerous cross-agent leakage and action conflicts by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the server filesystem and ingest uploaded files, while slim reads/writes filesystem artifacts and exposes stdin/stdout. No shared clipboard or MCP exists, but a shared server datastore and file-based handoff make prompt-like content from one agent plausibly influence the other. The pathway is interaction-based and not fully isolated.
conditions: IF Flowise writes attacker-controlled text into a shared file or datastore that slim later parses as commands or instructions
IF slim consumes Flowise-generated artifacts from stdin/stdout or files without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents onto distinct workspaces
Disable file-based handoff between agents
Add provenance labels to shared artifacts
Require manual review before slim consumes Flowise outputs
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and schema validation on shared channels

B_data_leakage.rationale: Flowise touches chatflow inputs/outputs and handles model provider keys and tool credentials, while slim touches container images, filesystem artifacts, environment variables, and certificate private keys. Flowise has broad network egress and file access, so a shared workspace or copied artifacts can leak sensitive data from slim into Flowise-connected services. The pairwise path is plausible and high impact.
conditions: IF slim processes images or files containing private keys, env vars, or certificates and those artifacts are exposed to Flowise
IF Flowise forwards chatflow inputs/outputs or uploaded files to external model providers or HTTP tools
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Run Flowise and slim under separate OS users
Redact keys and certificate material before handoff
Restrict Flowise network egress to approved endpoints
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning on shared artifacts

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Flowise can write the server filesystem and uses shared state via server datastore; slim can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, and write filesystem artifacts. Both therefore have overlapping write authority over mutable resources, and slim's privileged/container-oriented execution increases the chance of destructive interference if they target the same paths or state.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or Docker workspace
IF slim mutates files that Flowise also persists in its server datastore or filesystem
mitigations: Use separate writable directories
Mount shared paths read-only
Serialize access with a lock file
Run slim without privileged mode when possible
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level resource locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Flowise is a graph-based agent flow builder, so its outputs can become structured inputs to downstream nodes; slim is an interactive CLI that executes commands and analyzes targets. If Flowise-generated instructions or artifacts are fed into slim without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect container modifications or analysis results. The pair is not inherently self-verifying.
conditions: IF Flowise-generated text is passed into slim as commands, flags, or file paths
IF slim acts on Flowise outputs without an independent validation step
mitigations: Insert a human review step
Validate all paths and flags before execution
Use signed or schema-checked handoff files
Log and diff proposed actions before running slim
requires-engineering: add automated verification of Flowise outputs

E_compliance.rationale: Flowise handles chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets, while slim handles container images, environment variables, certificate private keys, and registry credentials. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch, but they do show different retention-sensitive data classes flowing through tools with different storage and execution models. That creates a compliance gap around retention and secret handling.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are stored in Flowise chatflows and then processed by slim
IF retention or deletion policies differ between Flowise server datastore and slim's temporary container artifacts
mitigations: Classify and segregate regulated data
Set explicit retention limits on shared artifacts
Avoid storing secrets in chatflow history
Document deletion procedures for both systems
requires-engineering: align retention and audit logging policies
